extractions.value: Lorish et al. proposed diagnostic criteria for stiff- person syndrome including: Stiffness and rigidity in axial muscles; Progression of stiffness to include proximal limb muscles; Abnormal axial posture (lumbar hyperlordosis); Superimposed episodic spasms precipitated by sudden movement, emotional upsets and unexpected auditory and somaesthetic stimuli (startle phenomenon); Absence of brainstem, pyramidal, extrapyramidal, and lower motor neuron (LMN) signs, sphincter and sensory disturbance, and cognitive involvement; Electromyography findings consistent with continuous motor unit activity in at least one axial muscle that may be abolished with administration of diazepam.

extractions.value: Male patient with anti-amphiphysin positive paraneoplastic SPS. Initial EMG was normal; subsequent EMG was consistent with SPS. Initial misdiagnoses included psychogenic dystonia and presumed Lyme disease. Malignancy (invasive ductal carcinoma of the left breast) was not detected until 3 years after symptom onset despite extensive screening. Significant SPS improvement occurred with cyclophosphamide (breast cancer chemotherapy) even before cancer was diagnosed.
